title: Network Topology Graph with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that renders an interactive 3D network topology graph with a physics debug overlay. Load the 'facecap.glb' model using GLTFLoader from the Three.js examples CDN and place it at the center of the network as the 'central server node'.

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (#0a0a1a) with a subtle grid floor (50x50, color #1a1a3a).
- PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 15, 30), looking at origin.
- AmbientLight (intensity 0.3) + DirectionalLight from (10,20,10) intensity 0.8.
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.

## Network Nodes
- Load 'facecap.glb' and scale it to roughly 2 units. Place at origin as the central hub node (id='hub').
- Create 8 satellite nodes as glowing spheres (radius 0.5) arranged in a circle of radius 12 around the hub at y=0. Use colors: 4 blue (#4488ff) nodes labeled 'server_0' to 'server_3', and 4 green (#44ff88) nodes labeled 'client_0' to 'client_3'.
- Each node should have a text sprite label above it showing its id.

## Edges (Connections)
- Draw lines (THREE.Line with LineBasicMaterial) connecting each satellite node to the hub. Lines should be colored based on 'traffic' value (green=low, yellow=medium, red=high).
- Also connect each server to 2 clients forming a ring-like sub-topology.
- Total edges should be 12 (8 hub connections + 4 server-client connections).

## Physics Simulation (Spring-Force Layout)
- Implement a simple force-directed layout: each node has velocity and position. Apply:
  - Repulsion force between all node pairs (Coulomb-like, strength 50)
  - Spring force along edges (rest length = 12 for hub edges, 8 for peer edges, spring constant 0.02)
  - Damping factor 0.95 per frame
  - Central gravity toward origin (strength 0.01)
- The physics runs each frame updating node positions. The hub node (facecap model) should also move according to physics unless pinned.
- Start with physics RUNNING.

## Debug Overlay
- Add a toggleable debug overlay (HTML div, id='debug-overlay') showing:
  - Total kinetic energy of the system
  - Number of nodes and edges
  - Average edge length
  - Whether physics is paused or running
  - FPS counter
- The overlay should have a semi-transparent dark background, positioned top-right.

## HUD / Controls (DOM buttons)
- Button id='btn-toggle-physics': Toggle physics simulation on/off. Text shows 'Pause Physics' or 'Resume Physics'.
- Button id='btn-toggle-debug': Toggle debug overlay visibility. Text: 'Toggle Debug'.
- Button id='btn-reset-layout': Reset all nodes to their initial circular positions and zero velocities.
- Button id='btn-pin-hub': Pin/unpin the hub node at origin. Text: 'Pin Hub' / 'Unpin Hub'.
- Button id='btn-add-traffic': Simulate traffic burst - randomize traffic values (0-1) on all edges, changing their colors.
- Button id='btn-highlight-path': Highlight shortest path from client_0 to client_2 by making those edges thick and bright white.
- Buttons should be styled in a vertical panel on the left side, dark themed.

## Keyboard Controls
- Press 'D' to toggle debug overlay (same as btn-toggle-debug).
- Press 'Space' to toggle physics (same as btn-toggle-physics).
- Press 'R' to reset layout.
- Press 'P' to pin/unpin hub.

## Click Interaction
- Clicking on a satellite node (raycasting) should select it, making it glow brighter (emissive intensity increase) and pinning it in place. Clicking again deselects and unpins it.
- Store the selected node id in state.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- modelLoaded: boolean, true once facecap.glb is loaded
- nodeCount: number (should be 9)
- edgeCount: number (should be 12)
- physicsRunning: boolean
- hubPinned: boolean
- debugVisible: boolean
- totalKineticEnergy: number (sum of 0.5 * |v|^2 for all nodes)
- averageEdgeLength: number
- selectedNodeId: string or null
- trafficBurstApplied: boolean (true after btn-add-traffic clicked)
- pathHighlighted: boolean (true after btn-highlight-path clicked)
- nodePositions: array of {id, x, y, z} for all 9 nodes
- hubPosition: {x, y, z}
- dampingFactor: 0.95
- frameCount: number incrementing each animation frame
- nodesHaveNaN: boolean (true if any node position is NaN - should always be false)
- fps: number

Ensure all values are updated in the animation loop BEFORE rendering.
physics_constraints: Force-directed spring layout: repulsion force inversely proportional to distance squared (strength 50), spring force proportional to displacement from rest length (k=0.02), damping 0.95 per frame, central gravity 0.01. Total kinetic energy should decay over time when no interaction occurs. No NaN values in any node position.
